werk/madonna-erotica.text:
Erotica was released on 19 October 1992, at the same time as Sex, Madonna's first book, and it was her first release on her own company, Maverick. For the record she worked once more with Shep Pettibone, known for Vogue, and with André Betts. Pettibone made the music, and Madonna wrote melodies and lyrics. Recording began in the autumn of 1991. The title track was recorded four times, and Fever was added only right at the end, when she began singing the old classic.

The album is about sex and love in the age of AIDS, and touches on themes such as sadomasochism and homophobia. It sounds different from her 1980s pop sound, drawing on hip hop, R&B, house and techno. She wrote In This Life in fifteen minutes, about a friend who had died. The first reactions were mixed, partly because of the uproar surrounding the book. Later, many critics came to rate the record more highly, and it has been cited as an influence on other female singers.
werk/madonna-erotica.listen: Listen to Deeper and Deeper and notice the flamenco guitar and the castanets in the middle of the song.

werk/madonna-like-a-prayer.text:
1988 was a difficult year for Madonna. Her film Who's That Girl flopped, the play Speed-the-Plow received poor reviews, and her marriage to Sean Penn fell apart. She turned thirty, the age at which her mother had died. She wanted to move away from slick teenage pop and make a more personal album about her Catholic upbringing, her marriage and her parents. She worked again with Patrick Leonard and Stephen Bray. Prince co-wrote and co-produced one track.

It is a pop record with rock and dance-pop elements. Recording ran from September 1988 to January 1989 in Los Angeles and at Paisley Park. Prince also played guitar, uncredited, on the title track among others. The reviews were unanimous in their praise for the introspective tone and the cohesion. Like a Prayer became her seventh number one on the US Hot 100, and Express Yourself reached number two. The record later came to be seen as a turning point: she was regarded as a serious artist rather than merely a pop star.
werk/madonna-like-a-prayer.listen: Listen to Like a Prayer and notice the guitar: it was played by Prince, even though his name was not on the record.

werk/madonna-like-a-virgin.text:
After her 1983 debut, Madonna wanted a sound of her own. Her label refused to let her produce herself, but did let her choose a producer. Her choice fell on Nile Rodgers, known for Chic and for David Bowie's Let's Dance. Recording took place at the Power Station in New York. Rodgers brought in his old Chic colleagues Bernard Edwards and Tony Thompson. Madonna chose all the songs herself: she wrote five of them, four of those with Stephen Bray.

Rodgers was doubtful about Like a Virgin at first, but the melody stayed in his head. Material Girl was written by others. Love Don't Live Here Anymore is a cover of Rose Royce, intended as a ballad to add variety. The reviews were mixed: the production was praised, the singing criticised. Even so, the album became her first number one on the US album chart. The title track became her first number one single. The record made her a superstar.
werk/madonna-like-a-virgin.listen: Listen to Love Don't Live Here Anymore, a Rose Royce cover that deliberately works as a ballad, giving a moment of calm and variety between the dance tracks.

werk/madonna-madonna.text:
In 1982 Madonna was living with Stephen Bray in a vacated rehearsal space in New York, where she made a demo tape of four dance tracks. DJ Mark Kamins played Everybody at the club Danceteria, and Sire Records signed her. Producer Reggie Lucas was brought in for the album, but she was not happy with his work. She therefore brought in her then boyfriend John Jellybean Benitez to produce and mix the rest. The sound is dance-pop and post-disco, with modern equipment such as the LinnDrum, Moog bass and Oberheim OB-X. She wrote Lucky Star herself, as a thank-you to Kamins. Holiday, originally written for the group Pure Energy, became her big breakthrough.

The first reviews were positive. In retrospect it is regarded as one of the best debut albums ever, one that made dance music popular again and gave dance-pop a standard.
werk/madonna-madonna.listen: Listen to Holiday and notice the drum machine and the synthesizers that carry the rhythm together: can you hear how danceable and light this sounds?

werk/madonna-ray-of-light.text:
After the birth of her daughter and her role in Evita, Madonna sought a new direction in 1997. She took an interest in Kabbalah, Hinduism and Buddhism and did yoga every day. The first sessions, with Babyface and Patrick Leonard, did not deliver what she wanted. She then began working with the English producer William Orbit. Recording took four and a half months, the longest of her career, and was delayed because Orbit's equipment kept failing.

The sound blends electronica, trip hop and techno-pop with dense analogue synthesizers and electric guitars. Only the title track, Ray of Light, is genuinely fast techno. Frozen and Drowned World/Substitute for Love combine electronic rhythms with orchestral sounds. The lyrics deal with fame, motherhood and spirituality. Critics praised the reinvention and Orbit's production, and the record won four Grammys, including Best Pop Album.
werk/madonna-ray-of-light.listen: Listen to Ray of Light. Notice the high tempo and the electronic rhythms, and hear how this is the only track on the album that really sounds like techno.

werk/madonna-true-blue.text:
After Like a Virgin, Madonna wanted to be seen as a serious artist with her third album. She recorded it in 1985 and 1986 and, for the first time, co-wrote and co-produced every track herself, together with Patrick Leonard and Stephen Bray. She had just married Sean Penn, and love and devotion recur throughout. The sound is pop and dance-pop with synthesizers, strings and drum machines, influenced by Motown, girl groups and Latin American music. Papa Don't Preach tells of a pregnant teenage girl who wants to keep her child, with baroque strings. La Isla Bonita blends flamenco guitar with Latin percussion. She also sings lower than before.

At the time of release, critics praised her growth as a singer, songwriter and producer. In retrospect the record is regarded as typical of 1980s music. The album reached number one in a record twenty-eight countries.
werk/madonna-true-blue.listen: Listen to La Isla Bonita and notice the flamenco guitar and the Latin percussion: how do they give this pop song an atmosphere all its own?

werk/magazine-real-life.text:
Real Life is the debut album by Magazine, an English post-punk band built around singer and lyricist Howard Devoto, formerly the frontman of the Buzzcocks. He wrote all the lyrics. The music took shape in the preceding year, mainly together with guitarist John McGeoch. The band recorded the album in March and April 1978 at Abbey Road Studios and in a Virgin mobile studio, with John Leckie as producer. The re-recorded version of Shot By Both Sides, the first single, is included, as is The Light Pours Out of Me, which Devoto wrote with Pete Shelley.

The album was released in June 1978 and received a great deal of praise. Critics lauded McGeoch's unpredictable guitar solos and the daring synthesizers of Dave Formula, which gave Devoto's bitter lyrics a grand sound. Real Life is regarded as a groundbreaking post-punk album and later featured on countless lists of the best albums, including in Uncut and Sounds.
werk/magazine-real-life.listen: In Shot By Both Sides, listen to how the sharp guitar and the synthesizers alternate while the vocals stay cool and detached.

werk/mahavishnu-orchestra-the-inner-moun.text:
Mahavishnu Orchestra was a five-piece group built around guitarist John McLaughlin that fused jazz and rock. After forming, the group first played a number of gigs before recording the debut album in August 1971. McLaughlin wrote all the tracks himself. The album was released later that year on Columbia, credited to the band and to the guitarist. The line-up also features Rick Laird on bass, Billy Cobham on drums, Jan Hammer on keyboards and Jerry Goodman on violin.

A JazzTimes reviewer heard classically inspired miniature suites in pieces such as Meeting of the Spirits and the acoustic A Lotus on Irish Streams. Awakening, driven by Cobham's blazing drums and the fierce, distorted guitar, appealed to rock audiences. Another reviewer called the album a wild, energetic meeting of virtuosos, which, a year after Bitches Brew, gave shape to the fusion of jazz and rock.
werk/mahavishnu-orchestra-the-inner-moun.listen: In A Lotus on Irish Streams, listen to how fragile and acoustic this piece sounds, and compare it with the distorted guitar in Awakening.

werk/mal-waldron-mal-2.text:
Mal/2 was released in November 1957 on Prestige. Mal Waldron recorded the album at the Van Gelder Studio in Hackensack, New Jersey, on 19 April and 17 May 1957, with a strong line-up. John Coltrane plays tenor sax, and Jackie McLean, Idrees Sulieman and Bill Hardman, among others, also take part.

The record contains Waldron's own compositions, such as J.M.'s Dream Doll and One by One, alongside standards such as From This Moment On and The Way You Look Tonight. According to AllMusic, the arrangements sound original and the record stands far above the many ordinary, blues-oriented hard bop albums of the period. The CD reissue added two tracks that had previously appeared on The Dealers.
werk/mal-waldron-mal-2.listen: In The Way You Look Tonight, listen to how the theme and the solos alternate.

werk/marc-almond-enchanted.text:
Enchanted is Marc Almond's sixth studio album and was released on 7 August 1990. It was recorded in various studios in London, with three producers: Bob Kraushaar and Gary Maughan each took half of the tracks, and Stephen Hague produced the first single, A Lover Spurned. The Desperate Hours and Waifs and Strays were also released as singles. Billy McGee, formerly of La Magia and the Willing Sinners, played on it, together with many session musicians.

The making of the album was difficult. In his autobiography the singer describes a conflict with Kraushaar: he wanted spontaneity and raw passion, whereas the producer preferred to rely on technique. A year later, the singer nevertheless found the result beautiful. The album reached number 52 in the UK, and A Lover Spurned entered the British Top 30. He calls the sleeve, with a photograph by Pierre et Gilles, his favourite.
werk/marc-almond-enchanted.listen: In A Lover Spurned, listen for the voice of the actress Julie T. Wallace, which can be heard alongside the singer.

werk/marc-almond-jacques.text:
Jacques is a tribute to the Belgian singer and writer Jacques Brel. The idea grew out of Marc Almond's collaboration with Paul Buck, who adapted Brel's original, non-English lyrics specially for him. It was his fifth studio album and was released in December 1989. The songs were recorded over a period of four years at Milo Studios in London.

He was helped by his own band, with Annie Hogan, Billy McGee and Steve Humphreys, and by various session musicians. Charles Gray produced and wrote the remaining arrangements. Annie Hogan plays piano, and cello, accordion, oboe and violin can also be heard. The sleeve is a painting by Johnny Deux.
werk/marc-almond-jacques.listen: In If You Go Away, listen to the string arrangements by Billy McGee and notice how they support the vocals.

werk/marc-almond-stories-of-johnny.text:
Stories of Johnny is Marc Almond's second studio album. It was released in September 1985 and reached number 22 on the UK album chart. Three singles were released from it, including the title track. The singer recorded the songs with his own group, The Willing Sinners, made up of Annie Hogan, Billy McGee, Martin McCarrick, Richard Riley and Steven Humphreys, supplemented by session musicians. Recording took place at Hartmann Digital Studios in Bavaria and in three studios in London.

Mike Hedges produced the record. The singer wrote all the arrangements himself. Besides piano, guitar, cello and bass, the instruments include a harp, a trumpet and a violin. Huw Feather designed the sleeve and Andy Catlin took the photographs.
werk/marc-almond-stories-of-johnny.listen: In Stories of Johnny, listen to the voice that tells the story and notice which instruments sound around it.

werk/marc-almond-the-stars-we-are.text:
The Stars We Are is Marc Almond's fourth studio album and was released in September 1988. It reached number 41 on the UK and number 144 on the US album chart and is his best-selling solo album. He recorded it at Matrix Studios in London, with his group La Magia and various guest musicians. Four singles came from it, including Tears Run Rings, his only solo record to reach the US Hot 100.

The album includes Your Kisses Burn, a duet with Nico recorded shortly before her death. The duet with Gene Pitney on Something's Gotten Hold of My Heart was recorded only after the album's release. It became a number one in the United Kingdom in early 1989 and was subsequently added to the CD and cassette.
werk/marc-almond-the-stars-we-are.listen: In Your Kisses Burn, listen to how Nico's voice and the singer's relate to one another: this duet was recorded shortly before her death.

werk/marco-borsato-dromen-zijn-bedrog.text: In 1994 Marco Borsato had an enormous hit with Dromen zijn bedrog, a Dutch version of an Italian song. It stayed at number one for weeks. Borsato became the best-selling Dutch singer of his time, with big ballads in Dutch and sold-out stadium concerts. Critics found his music slick, but he showed how large the audience for Dutch-language song was.
werk/marco-borsato-dromen-zijn-bedrog.listen: Listen for the big ballad with strings and a chorus that keeps climbing higher. Made to be sung along to at full volume.

werk/marillion-clutching-at-straws.text:
Clutching at Straws was released on 22 June 1987 and is the fourth studio album by the British neo-prog band. It was the last with singer Fish, who left in 1988. The album is a concept album about Torch, an unemployed twenty-nine-year-old man who tries to forget his failed marriage and his failed singing career in drink, in bars and in hotel rooms. Incommunicado is about pressure from the record company.

The album sold less than its predecessor, Misplaced Childhood, but still entered the British chart at number two. Incommunicado, Sugar Mice and Warm Wet Circles reached the British top forty. Critics praised the music. AllMusic called it an underrated masterpiece, and Rolling Stone included it in a 2015 list of the best prog albums, with praise for the atmospheric production and the spacious guitar playing of Steve Rothery.
werk/marillion-clutching-at-straws.listen: Listen to Warm Wet Circles and notice Steve Rothery's spacious, understated guitar playing.

werk/marillion-fugazi.text:
Fugazi is Marillion's second studio album, released in 1984. Nick Tauber produced it, and it was recorded in various studios between November 1983 and February 1984. The band was behind schedule and EMI was applying pressure. After the dismissal of Mick Pointer, several drummers had come and gone, and Ian Mosley was the first drummer to play on this album. The tour began before the record was finished.

According to AllMusic, the album sounds more direct and more like hard rock than the previous one. Reviewers single out Assassing, Incubus and Fugazi, songs that remained concert favourites for years. Punch and Judy and Assassing became hits, and the album reached the British top five and went gold. Guitarist Steve Rothery later felt that the guitars sounded too bright. Mark Wilkinson's sleeve was named by Gigwise as one of the best album covers of all time.
werk/marillion-fugazi.listen: Listen to Assassing and notice how bright and glossy the sound is, something guitarist Rothery later found too bright.

werk/marillion-misplaced-childhood.text:
Misplaced Childhood is Marillion's third studio album and was released on 17 June 1985. The group recorded it in the spring at Hansa Tonstudio in Berlin, with producer Chris Kimsey, who had previously worked for the Rolling Stones. It is their first true concept album, with one continuous piece of music on each side of the LP. Singer Fish came up with the story during a ten-hour LSD trip. It is loosely about his youth and revolves around lost love, sudden success and the loss of childhood, with a hopeful ending.

Kayleigh is a ballad with guitar, and Lavender is a piano-led song partly based on the folk song Lavender Blue. Both became big hits. Heart of Lothian refers to Fish's region of Scotland. The album went straight to number one in Great Britain and is the group's most successful record. In 2003 Classic Rock ranked it fourth in a list of the best concept albums.
werk/marillion-misplaced-childhood.listen: Listen to Lavender and notice how the piano and the gentle melody evoke the innocence of childhood.

werk/marillion-script-for-a-jester-s-tea.text:
Marillion released their debut album on 14 March 1983 on EMI. Recording ran from December 1982 to February 1983 at Marquee Studios in London. Producer David Hitchcock was injured in a car accident after the single Market Square Heroes, whereupon EMI persuaded the band to work with Nick Tauber, who was seen as more modern. Fish wrote all the lyrics. It was the only studio album with founder and drummer Mick Pointer. Mark Wilkinson designed the sleeve.

The album produced two British hits, He Knows You Know and Garden Party, and reached number 7 on the UK album chart. Dave Dickson of Kerrang! thought it very impressive as a debut, and Prog Magazine places it at number 40 on its list of the hundred best prog albums. Fish and guitarist Steve Rothery both speak critically of it later: Fish about his forced singing, Rothery about his guitar sound.
werk/marillion-script-for-a-jester-s-tea.listen: Listen to Script For a Jester's Tear and notice the vocals of Fish, who wrote all the lyrics on the album.

werk/marillion-seasons-end.text:
Seasons End was released in 1989 and is the first album with singer Steve Hogarth, after Fish left the band at the end of 1988. The group looked for a new singer while already writing the album. As a result, the music was largely finished before Hogarth arrived. He contributed only partly to Easter and The Space. Many of the lyrics were written by John Helmer. The producer was Nick Davis, and the band recorded at Outside Studios in Oxfordshire.

Unlike on the two previous albums, the lyrics do not form a continuous story. The King of Sunset Town refers to the crushing of the protests in Tiananmen Square, Easter is about the Troubles in Northern Ireland, and Berlin about the divided city, whose Wall fell a few weeks after the album came out. The album reached number seven in the UK. A Kerrang! critic felt that Hogarth had a voice of his own.
werk/marillion-seasons-end.listen: Listen to Easter and notice Steve Rothery's long guitar solo in the album version, which is cut down sharply in the single version.

werk/mark-knopfler-cal.text:
Cal is Mark Knopfler's second soundtrack album and was released on 24 August 1984. The music accompanies the film Cal from the same year, directed by Pat O'Connor and produced by David Puttnam. Puttnam also produced Local Hero from 1983, the film for which the guitarist had previously written music.

All the music is by him. In The New York Times, Janet Maslin called the record an exceptionally beautiful and haunting score. AllMusic later described it as a quiet, thoughtful series of pieces that does not seek false drama but supports the story. In 2013 he played Father and Son on tour as an instrumental introduction to Hill Farmer's Blues, which shows that the music stayed with him for a long time.
werk/mark-knopfler-cal.listen: Listen to Father and Son and notice how restrained and undramatic this instrumental piece remains.

werk/mark-knopfler-golden-heart.text:
After the last Dire Straits tour in 1992, Mark Knopfler put an end to the band. A world tour with 7.1 million visitors had placed a heavy strain on his work and private life, and he said that such a scale is dehumanising. He recovered for two years and in 1994 began work on his first solo record, which appeared in 1996.

The album draws on the musical influences of his whole career, with an acoustic bass, string arrangements and traditional Irish accompaniment. Darling Pretty was the first single and featured in the film Twister. In sound and structure, Cannibals strongly resembles the Dire Straits song Walk of Life. AllMusic found the record listenable but second-hand: Knopfler was said not to have challenged himself.
werk/mark-knopfler-golden-heart.listen: Listen to Cannibals and compare it with what you know of Walk of Life. What sounds the same, and what is slightly different?

werk/mark-knopfler-sailing-to-philadelph.text:
On his second solo album, released in September 2000, Mark Knopfler brought in guest singers. James Taylor and Van Morrison sing along, as do Chris Difford and Glenn Tilbrook of Squeeze on one version of the album. For seventeen years Knopfler had mainly made soundtracks and roots projects.

The title song comes from the novel Mason & Dixon by Thomas Pynchon, about the two English surveyors who drew the border between Pennsylvania and Maryland in the 1760s. Taylor sings that duet. In The Last Laugh, Morrison trades lines with Knopfler. Rolling Stone called the record a welcome look back at the best period of Dire Straits. By 2002 it had sold more than 3.5 million copies.
werk/mark-knopfler-sailing-to-philadelph.listen: Listen to The Last Laugh and notice how the voices of Van Morrison and Knopfler alternate line by line.

werk/marlena-shaw-from-the-depths-of-my-.text:
From the Depths of My Soul is an album by the American singer Marlena Shaw. She recorded it in 1973 and it was released on the Blue Note label. Recording took place on 30 and 31 May, and strings were added on 6 June. The arrangements and direction were by Wade Marcus.

The record contains eleven songs by various songwriters, including Randy Edelman, Bob Dorough, Charles Fox and Norman Gimbel. She wrote Say a Good Word herself. She was accompanied by a large group of musicians, including pianist Derek Smith, bassist Ron Carter, guitarist Cornell Dupree and drummer Grady Tate, supplemented by harp, horns and strings.
werk/marlena-shaw-from-the-depths-of-my-.listen: Listen to Say a Good Word, the only song the singer wrote herself. Notice how her voice carries the song.

werk/marlena-shaw-the-spice-of-life.text:
The Spice of Life is the second album by singer Marlena Shaw and her last studio record for Cadet Records. Richard Evans and Charles Stepney arranged and produced it, and Bobby Miller supervised the album. The record was released in 1969 and contains ten tracks.

It includes covers of Call It Stormy Monday by T-Bone Walker, Go Away Little Boy by Gerry Goffin and Carole King, and Anyone Can Move a Mountain. There is also original work, such as Woman of the Ghetto and Liberation Conversation, which she wrote together with Bobby Miller. Best known is her version of California Soul, a song by Ashford and Simpson. This was the first time she recorded Go Away Little Boy.
werk/marlena-shaw-the-spice-of-life.listen: Listen to California Soul and notice how Shaw's voice stands at the front of the arrangement.

werk/martin-garrix-animals.text: In June 2013, Animals by seventeen-year-old Martin Garrix from Amstelveen was released. The track became a hit across Europe and a staple at festivals. Garrix had made it at home, in his bedroom studio. In the same year Hardwell was voted the world's best DJ. With Tiësto, Armin van Buuren and Afrojack, Dutch producers shaped a large part of dance music.
werk/martin-garrix-animals.listen: Animals has almost no vocals. Listen for the drop: a bare, hard synthesizer riff over a stomping beat.

werk/marvin-gaye-hello-broadway.text:
Hello Broadway is Marvin Gaye's fourth studio album and was released in 1964. It consists of standards and numbers from Broadway musicals. In those years Gaye was growing into Motown's most important male solo star.

The record shows that he himself would rather have been a crooner in the style of Nat King Cole and Frank Sinatra than the R&B hitmaker that Motown wanted him to be. The label's management wanted him to target a young R&B audience, not an adult one. Gene Page made the arrangements. This places the album in a series in which Gaye still strongly imitates Cole's voice. It would be years before he made a standards album that was more his own. A comparable record by another Motown group is On Broadway by the Four Tops.
werk/marvin-gaye-hello-broadway.listen: Listen to People and notice how Gaye sings here in a soft, smooth voice, and how far that is from his R&B singles.

werk/marvin-gaye-in-the-groove.text:
In the Groove was released on 26 August 1968 on Tamla, Marvin Gaye's first solo album in two years. In the meantime he had become best known as a duet partner of, among others, Kim Weston and Tammi Terrell. Motown brought him back to the studio in early 1967. Producer Norman Whitfield and his protégé Frank Wilson wrote songs that suited Gaye's restless life. Terrell became seriously ill in late 1967, which weighed heavily on him.

The best-known track is I Heard It Through the Grapevine. Whitfield pushed Gaye to sing higher than he was used to. Berry Gordy at first did not want to release the song, so You and Chained came out first as a single. When Grapevine was released after all in October 1968, it became a number one. Motown then reissued the album under that title. Gaye also tried his hand as a producer for the first time here and wrote songs himself. The reviews were generally positive.
werk/marvin-gaye-in-the-groove.listen: Listen to I Heard It Through the Grapevine and notice Gaye's singing voice: it sits higher than you would expect from him. Hear, too, how tense and urgent that sounds.

werk/marvin-gaye-let-s-get-it-on.text:
After the success of What's Going On, Marvin Gaye was given more creative freedom by Motown, but in 1972 he struggled with writer's block. He was also unsure whether to move to Los Angeles, now that Berry Gordy was relocating the label there. Recording ran from 1970 to 1973, in Detroit and Los Angeles. Where his previous album had been about politics, he now used love and sex as an image for a deeper quest, in an attempt to come to terms with his strict upbringing.

It is his first foray into funk, mixed with gentle soul and doo-wop, and with sensual lyrics. Gaye layers several vocal registers on top of one another. The singles Let's Get It On, Come Get to This and You Sure Love to Ball reached the charts. It became his most commercially successful album at Motown. The title track helped launch the slow jam and the quiet storm format, and later R&B artists drew inspiration from the album.
werk/marvin-gaye-let-s-get-it-on.listen: In Let's Get It On, listen to Gaye's soft, seductive singing and to the vocal layers with which he accompanies himself.

werk/marvin-gaye-midnight-love.text:
Marvin Gaye was angry about how Motown had released his album In Our Lifetime and wanted never to record there again. In early 1981 he moved to the Belgian town of Ostend, where the concert promoter Freddy Cousaert helped him kick his drug habit. There he prepared his comeback, with a new band. He began work on the new album in December 1981 in Brussels. On 23 March 1982 he signed with Columbia. He wanted to make more mainstream music: 'I need a hit,' he said.

Midnight Love was released on 8 November 1982, the last album to appear in his lifetime. It was an immediate international success and produced the hit Sexual Healing, which won two Grammys. The album was nominated for a Grammy and was named Album of the Year for 1982 by the NME. Rolling Stone placed it at number 37 among the best albums of the 1980s.
werk/marvin-gaye-midnight-love.listen: Listen to Sexual Healing and notice the relaxed, danceable mood of the song. Hear how it fits what Gaye himself called a party record, yet with a personal undertone.

werk/marvin-gaye-that-stubborn-kinda-fel.text:
After his first album, a mixture of jazz and blues that failed to catch on, Marvin Gaye and Motown had to decide afresh which direction his career should take. The success of The Marvelettes with Please Mr. Postman and of the song Beechwood 4-5789, which he co-wrote, convinced him to try a younger R&B sound. Together with Mickey Stevenson he wrote new songs.

The record was released in December 1962 on Tamla and, like many Motown albums of the time, was made quickly. The house band, later known as the Funk Brothers, played the music; Martha and the Vandellas sang the backing vocals. R&B, blues, doo-wop and early soul run together. Stubborn Kind of Fellow became his first hit single, Pride and Joy his first pop top ten. The album brought Gaye into the circle of Motown's hitmakers and later became beloved of British mods and Northern Soul fans.
werk/marvin-gaye-that-stubborn-kinda-fel.listen: In Pride and Joy, listen to the backing vocals that answer the lead vocal.

werk/marvin-gaye-what-s-going-on.text:
In the late 1960s Marvin Gaye was deeply depressed. His singing partner Tammi Terrell died in 1970, his marriage had collapsed and he was struggling with cocaine and with Motown. He withdrew and grew a beard. When Renaldo Benson of the Four Tops offered him a song written after police violence against demonstrators in Berkeley, Gaye saw a message in it. Recording ran from 1970 to 1971, including at Hitsville U.S.A. in Detroit. For the first time he was his own producer, with the regular Motown session musicians, the Funk Brothers.

The songs flow into one another, like a song cycle from the perspective of a Vietnam veteran returning home to a country full of hatred and injustice. It deals with drugs, poverty and war, and in Mercy Mercy Me (The Ecology) already with the environment. The album was an immediate success and is regarded as a classic of soul.
werk/marvin-gaye-what-s-going-on.listen: Listen to the title track and notice how soft and warm the singing sounds, while the question in the lyrics grows ever more urgent.

werk/mary-hopkin-earth-song-ocean-song.text:
Mary Hopkin had had enough of the pop songs that had made her famous. In 1971 she asked producer Tony Visconti, known for an album by the Strawbs, for an acoustic album with strings. Visconti brought in folk musicians: Dave Cousins, Ralph McTell and Danny Thompson. Recording began in May 1971 at AIR Studios in London. It was her second album, more than two years after Post Card.

Hopkin chose her songs from some two hundred titles. There are two songs by McTell on it, including Streets of London, as well as The Wind by Cat Stevens and How Come the Sun by Tom Paxton. Visconti wanted to use modern techniques for a super-folk sound. The reviews were glowing, but the album was not a commercial success, partly because Hopkin could not promote it owing to her summer shows. It was her last album for eighteen years.
werk/mary-hopkin-earth-song-ocean-song.listen: Listen to Streets of London and notice how little is needed: her voice, the acoustic guitar and a gentle accompaniment.

werk/mary-hopkin-post-card.text:
In 1968 Mary Hopkin appeared on the TV programme Opportunity Knocks. Twiggy saw her and pointed her out to Paul McCartney, who signed her to Apple Records, the Beatles' label. After the worldwide hit Those Were the Days, they made her debut album together, recorded from October to early December 1968 at EMI Studios, among other places. It was released in February 1969 and reached number 3 in the United Kingdom.

The album features old showtunes such as Lullaby of the Leaves and Someone to Watch Over Me, favourites of McCartney's father. Hopkin herself felt that some songs were too mature for her voice. Three songs were written by Donovan, who also plays acoustic guitar: Lord of the Reedy River, Voyage of the Moon and Happiness Runs. Harry Nilsson wrote The Puppy Song. She sings in Welsh in Y Blodyn Gwyn and in French in Prince en Avignon. The sleeve shows a photograph by Linda Eastman.
werk/mary-hopkin-post-card.listen: Listen to Lord of the Reedy River and notice how Hopkin's clear voice sounds above Donovan's acoustic guitar.

werk/mary-j-blige-mary.text:
Mary was released on 17 August 1999 on MCA Records. It was Mary J. Blige's fourth album, and as on Share My World she was executive producer. She let go of the obvious hip hop influences of her earlier work and opted for classic soul, with smooth productions reminiscent of the 1970s. This surprised many fans and critics. She worked with, among others, Lauryn Hill, Jadakiss, Eric Clapton, Elton John, K-Ci and George Michael. I'm In Love, As and Let No Man Put Asunder are covers of The Gap Band, Stevie Wonder and First Choice.

The album entered at number two on the Billboard 200 and produced five charting singles. The reviews were glowing. Spin heard blues moans, gospel and jazz, and Q praised her transitions from bravado to vulnerability. Soren Baker felt the strength lay above all in how she sings the songs.
werk/mary-j-blige-mary.listen: Listen to Deep Inside. Notice how the vocals carry the song.

werk/mary-j-blige-share-my-world.text:
In 1997 Mary J. Blige faced major changes. She moved from Uptown to MCA and broke with her regular producer and mentor Sean Combs. For the album she brought in a series of producers, including Rodney Jerkins, Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis, Babyface and R. Kelly. The record leans less on hip hop soul than her first two and more on R&B. It was her third album and the first on which she worked as executive producer. Guests include Lil' Kim, Nas, George Benson and Roy Ayers.

After the dark My Life, she reportedly worked towards a healthier life, and you can hear that in the lighter mood. Share My World went straight to number one in the United States. Alex Henderson of AllMusic praised its character and honesty, and Rolling Stone heard real singing. Other critics found it uneven.
werk/mary-j-blige-share-my-world.listen: Listen to Not Gon' Cry. Notice how the singer lets you hear pain and control at the same time.

werk/mary-j-blige-what-s-the-411.text:
At seventeen, Mary J. Blige sang a cover of Caught Up in the Rapture on a tape in a shopping mall. Via an employee of Uptown Records it ended up with director Andre Harrell, who signed her in 1990. The debut album was released on 28 July 1992, with Sean Combs as executive producer and contributions from, among others, DeVante Swing, Dave Hall and Mark Morales.

The title refers to her former job as a 411 telephone operator. The album opens with Leave A Message, answering-machine messages over a drum beat. The music blends hip hop, R&B and new jack swing, with a singer who comes across as tough and sings raw lyrics. You Remind Me and Real Love reached number 1 on the R&B chart. Critics praised her voice and the combination of hip hop and soul, and the album later came to be seen as the beginning of hip hop soul.
werk/mary-j-blige-what-s-the-411.listen: Listen to Leave A Message and notice the spoken messages over the drum beat, before the first real songs begin.

werk/mary-lou-williams-zoning.text:
Zoning is a studio album by the pianist Mary Lou Williams, released in 1974 by Mary Records. She arranged the music herself and plays in duo and trio, mainly with bassist Bob Cranshaw and drummer Mickey Roker. The pieces vary greatly in mood: dreamy in an Ellington manner in Ghost of Love, with communal shouts in Praise the Lord, and funky in Play It Momma. In Zoning Fungus II she uses atonal harmonies before the piece settles on a steady funky bass.

The album was well received on release. Gary Giddins chose it in his Village Voice column as one of the ten best albums of the year. In 1995 Smithsonian Folkways reissued it on CD, with a different track listing and two previously unreleased recordings.
werk/mary-lou-williams-zoning.listen: In Zoning Fungus II, listen to the atonal harmonies at the beginning and hear how the piece then lands on a steady funky bass.

werk/massive-attack-blue-lines.text:
Blue Lines is the debut by Massive Attack and was released in April 1991. The group from Bristol worked on it for about eight months, with Jonny Dollar as co-producer. Many of the ideas were already years old, dating from the days of The Wild Bunch and the Bristol sound systems. Neneh Cherry got the group working, and part of it was recorded at her home. Singers Shara Nelson and Horace Andy contributed to the record.

The sound blends hip hop, dub, soul, reggae and electronic music into dance music for the head rather than the feet. The tempos are low, sometimes only 67 beats per minute. Blue Lines is regarded as the first album of what would later be called trip hop. Critics called it a blueprint for that style, and according to The Guardian it still sounds unique. Unfinished Sympathy received a great deal of praise. In 1991 the record reached number 13 on the UK album chart.
werk/massive-attack-blue-lines.listen: Listen to Unfinished Sympathy and notice how Shara Nelson's voice rises above the slow, nocturnal rhythm.

werk/massive-attack-mezzanine.text:
For Mezzanine, Robert Del Naja wanted a darker sound in 1997. He made instrumental demos with samples of British post-punk bands such as Wire and Gang of Four, far removed from the jazzy soul of the previous records Blue Lines and Protection. The sessions were tense and almost broke the group apart. The release was pushed back four months to April 1998. Andrew Vowles left shortly afterwards. For the first time Del Naja worked with producer Neil Davidge, and Tricky no longer took part.

The result is a trip hop and electronica record full of claustrophobic atmosphere, heavy bass and abstract sounds. Horace Andy sings on several tracks, and Elizabeth Fraser of Cocteau Twins also sings. Inertia Creeps builds on a rhythm from Turkish music that Del Naja recorded after a night out in Istanbul. Critics were full of praise for the dark sound. Several magazines place the record among the best albums of the 1990s.
werk/massive-attack-mezzanine.listen: Listen to Inertia Creeps and notice the bass and the effects that together create a menacing, shadowy atmosphere. Hear how little the track needs to build tension.

werk/matmos-a-chance-to-cut-is-a-chance-.text:
A Chance to Cut Is a Chance to Cure is the fourth studio album by the American duo Matmos, released in 2001. Drew Daniel and Martin Schmidt both have doctors for parents, which presumably influenced the choice of theme. The album consists mainly of samples of medical procedures: plastic surgery, liposuction, hearing tests and bone saws. Despite the gravity of the material, the tone remains humorous.

The only exception is For Felix (and All the Rats), a piece for their late pet rat Felix, played entirely on his cage. The album has been called a concept album within glitch and musique concrète. AllMusic spoke of seven accessible, melodic pieces of experimental techno. Simon Reynolds wrote in Spin about the surrealism of the beauty industry. In 2017 Pitchfork placed it at number 19 on its list of the best IDM albums of all time.
werk/matmos-a-chance-to-cut-is-a-chance-.listen: Listen to For Felix (and All the Rats) and try to hear that the sounds come from a rat's cage.

werk/matmos-matmos.text:
This is the debut album by the American duo Matmos, released in 1997. The music is experimental and electronic, with influences from drum and bass, minimal techno and glitch. What makes the record special is the material the duo worked with: field recordings of everyday actions and of unusual sound sources. On Verber: Amplified Synapse, for instance, you can hear the nerve activity of a crayfish.

The eleven tracks range from short sketches to longer pieces, with titles such as Plastic Minor, Lunaire and Office Furniture (After Evidence). With this approach, turning everyday sounds into electronic music, Matmos laid the foundation for the work the duo would go on to make. On the next album, Quasi-Objects from 1998, the duo continued along the same path.
werk/matmos-matmos.listen: Listen to Verber: Amplified Synapse and try to hear how a sound from nature has been turned into electronic music.

werk/matmos-quasi-objects.text:
Quasi-Objects was released in 1998 as the follow-up to Matmos's self-titled debut. The duo built the music from ordinary sounds that it recorded in and around its own home. Drew Daniel and M.C. Schmidt used, among other things, latex clothing, balloons, a whoopee cushion and sounds from their own bodies, alongside banjo, electric guitar, sampler and synthesizers. Schmidt also made the illustration on the sleeve.

The record thus continued along the path set by the debut: experimental electronic music made from everyday sounds. The reception was mixed. AllMusic found the album both an improvement and a disappointment, because the idea of making tracks from strange sounds took over. Pitchfork found the record too dependent on its gimmicky premise.
werk/matmos-quasi-objects.listen: Listen to Latex and notice which everyday sounds you recognise among the electronic textures.

werk/matmos-the-civil-war.text:
The Civil War is the fifth studio album by the experimental duo Matmos and was released on Matador Records. It explores the boundary between Americana, medieval folk music and electronics. Striking is the large number of real instruments, such as drums, brass and guitars. A hurdy-gurdy is also sampled, and the piece The Stars and Stripes Forever receives a satirical treatment.

The title fits the contrasts in the music. AllMusic gave the album 4.5 out of 5 stars and spoke of a title that reflects the inner contradictions of the sound. Pitchfork called it the group's best work, both as a technical achievement and as pure sound. On Metacritic the album scored 77 points based on 22 reviews, indicating generally favourable reviews.
werk/matmos-the-civil-war.listen: Listen to The Stars and Stripes Forever and notice where the familiar march is altered or twisted.

werk/maurice-jarre-lawrence-of-arabia.text:
The music for the 1962 film Lawrence of Arabia did not come about easily. Director David Lean first thought of Malcolm Arnold, but Arnold did not think much of the film, together with William Walton. Producer Sam Spiegel then brought in Richard Rodgers, but Lean called his work nonsense. The young Frenchman Maurice Jarre had meanwhile written a theme that Lean liked so much that he let him score the whole film. Jarre had six weeks. The London Philharmonic Orchestra played the music at Shepperton Studios, with three ondes Martenot, among other instruments.

As with The Bridge on the River Kwai, Lean wanted to use a march by Kenneth Alford: The Voice of the Guns, which sounds in the overture and in fragments throughout the film. The score won the Oscar for Best Original Score and is regarded as one of the best film scores ever. In 2005 the American Film Institute ranked it third.
werk/maurice-jarre-lawrence-of-arabia.listen: Listen to Overture and try to recognise the march The Voice of the Guns, which is woven into the overture.

werk/max-martin-baby-one-more-time.text: Max Martin first wrote ...Baby One More Time for the Backstreet Boys and the American group TLC, who both turned it down. It then went to sixteen-year-old Britney Spears, and it was released in October 1998. By hit me, Martin probably meant something like call me one more time. The song became a worldwide hit. Denniz PoP, his mentor at Cheiron, did not live to see its success: he died in August 1998.
werk/max-martin-baby-one-more-time.listen: The song opens with three heavy piano notes and then straight into the voice: Oh baby, baby. The hook is there within the first seconds.

werk/max-richter-infra.text:
Infra was released on 19 July 2010 on FatCat Records and reissued by Deutsche Grammophon in 2014. Max Richter, a composer of neoclassical music, plays piano and electronics himself and mixed the record. Two violins, a viola and two cellos accompany him. The sleeve comes from the backdrop of the production of the same name by The Royal Ballet at the Royal Opera House in London in 2008.

The album received mostly positive reviews and averaged 77 on Metacritic from 14 reviews. Joe Tangari of Pitchfork wrote that even without knowledge of its origins, Infra is an enveloping and moving work. In his view it is some of Richter's best music, and every listener brings their own feeling to it. The tracks are titled Infra or Journey, numbered throughout the record.
werk/max-richter-infra.listen: Listen to Infra 1 and notice what the piano, the electronics and the strings are each doing.

werk/max-richter-memoryhouse.text:
Memoryhouse, from 2002, is the debut album by the neoclassical composer Max Richter. It was first released on the label Late Junction and reissued in 2009 and 2014 on FatCat Records, with different sleeve designs. Richter recorded it with the BBC Philharmonic Orchestra under conductor Rumon Gamba. There are solo parts for violin, cello and soprano, and the music is supplemented by spoken texts by John Cage and Marina Tsvetaeva. Richter wrote the music, produced the record and mixed it himself.

The record received mostly positive reviews. For the 2014 reissue, Pitchfork again wrote a very positive assessment.
werk/max-richter-memoryhouse.listen: Listen to Sarajevo and notice how orchestra and soloists together build a restrained, sombre atmosphere. Which instruments do you hear most clearly?

werk/max-richter-recomposed-by-max-richt.text:
Recomposed by Max Richter is a complete rewriting of Vivaldi's violin concertos The Four Seasons. Richter said that he had left out 75 per cent of the original material. What he does use is shifted and repeated in phases, making his background in minimal music and postmodernism audible. The album was released on 31 August 2012 on Deutsche Grammophon, played by violinist Daniel Hope with the Konzerthaus Kammerorchester Berlin under André de Ridder.

Hope plays the Ex-Lipinski, a 1742 Guarneri del Gesù violin. The record topped the iTunes classical chart in the United Kingdom, Germany and the United States. Ivan Hewett of The Telegraph wrote that the friction between Richter's repeating patterns and those of Vivaldi produces an ambiguous colour. The piece received its first UK performance on 31 October 2012 at the Barbican Centre.
werk/max-richter-recomposed-by-max-richt.listen: Listen to Spring 1 and notice how Richter's repeating patterns relate to Vivaldi's melody.

werk/max-richter-songs-from-before.text:
Songs from Before is the third solo album by the neoclassical composer Max Richter. It was released on 23 October 2006 on 130701, a sub-label of FatCat Records, and reissued by Deutsche Grammophon in 2014. Richter plays piano himself, with cello and violin from other musicians. What makes the record special are the texts from novels by Haruki Murakami, read aloud by Robert Wyatt, including from Norwegian Wood and Sputnik Sweetheart. They return in tracks such as Flowers for Yulia, Harmonium and Verses.

The reviews were mostly positive. Pitchfork wrote that Richter adapts techniques from classical music and lets his heroes and memories show openly, in keeping with the nostalgia that lies at the heart of the record.
werk/max-richter-songs-from-before.listen: Listen to Harmonium and notice how Robert Wyatt's spoken text relates to the music beneath it. What does his voice do to the atmosphere?

werk/max-roach-award-winning-drummer.text:
Award Winning Drummer is an album by drummer Max Roach with a 1958 session, released on the label Time. The album also appeared under the title Max Roach. Roach plays here with an unusual line-up: Booker Little on trumpet, George Coleman on tenor saxophone, Ray Draper on tuba and Art Davis on bass. There is no piano.

The repertoire is partly by Roach himself, such as Tuba de Nod and Pies of Quincy. There are also pieces by band members: Coleman wrote Variations on the Scene and Sadiga, and Little wrote Gandolfo's Bounce. Milano is by John Lewis, and Old Folks is a standard by Dedette Lee Hill and Willard Robison. Ron Wynn of AllMusic called the group one of the best hard bop ensembles there is.
werk/max-roach-award-winning-drummer.listen: Listen to Tuba de Nod and notice the role of Ray Draper's tuba alongside Roach's drums.

werk/max-roach-deeds-not-words.text:
Deeds, Not Words contains 1958 recordings by drummer Max Roach and was released on the label Riverside. Roach led a quintet with trumpeter Booker Little, tuba player Ray Draper, tenor saxophonist George Coleman and bassist Art Davis. The combination with a tuba is unusual in the jazz of the time. The record contains standards such as You Stepped Out of a Dream and There Will Never Be Another You, but also original pieces by the band members, such as Filidé by Draper and Larry-Larue by Little. The CD version has an extra track with bassist Oscar Pettiford.

AllMusic gave the album four and a half stars and called it good music from a group that wanted to develop beyond hard bop.
werk/max-roach-deeds-not-words.listen: Listen to Filidé and notice Ray Draper's tuba alongside the trumpet: how does that combination sound in the ensemble?

werk/mc-solaar-prose-combat.text:
Prose Combat is the second studio album by the French rapper MC Solaar. It was released in 1994 on Cohiba Records and brought him international fame. Jimmy Jay handled production and scratching, Boom Bass scratching and sampling, and bassist Laurent Vernerey played on it. A track left over from the sessions, Comme dans un film, later ended up on the album of music inspired by the film La Haine.

The album opens with Aubade, a piece of less than a minute. Nouveau western is built on a sample of Bonnie and Clyde by Serge Gainsbourg, who is also credited as a writer. The British release has a different track listing: three tracks were replaced and the order was changed.
werk/mc-solaar-prose-combat.listen: In Nouveau western, listen to the sample of Bonnie and Clyde by Serge Gainsbourg and notice how the rap sits against it.

werk/mc-solaar-qui-seme-le-vent-recolte-.text:
Qui sème le vent récolte le tempo is the debut album by the French rapper MC Solaar, released in 1991. The title is a pun on the French proverb Qui sème le vent récolte la tempête, which goes back to the Book of Hosea in the Bible. The album was very successful.

Bouge de là was the first single and grew into a big hit in France, launching his career. The track is built on a sample of The Message by the English band Cymande. The title track uses a sample of One Cylinder by Lou Donaldson. Caroline and Victime de la mode also became popular singles. The album also contains two instrumental pieces, Intro and Funky Dreamer, and a few improvised tracks.
werk/mc-solaar-qui-seme-le-vent-recolte-.listen: In Bouge de là, Pt. 1, listen to the sample of The Message by Cymande and notice how the rap sits on top of it.

werk/mccoy-tyner-the-real-mccoy.text:
The Real McCoy came about at a difficult time for pianist McCoy Tyner. Two years earlier he had left John Coltrane's quartet, and he even considered saying goodbye to jazz and becoming a taxi driver. On 21 April 1967 he recorded this album, his seventh and his first for the Blue Note label. With him played tenor saxophonist Joe Henderson, bassist Ron Carter and drummer Elvin Jones, who had also played with Coltrane. Producer Alfred Lion spoke of a pure jazz session.

The pianist chose the modal, rhythmically complex direction that the Coltrane quartet had taken before 1965. Passion Dance recalls a trance-like dance, and Contemplation sounds like a man alone, reflecting on religion and on life. Blues on the Corner is a cheerful portrait of his youth in Philadelphia. One reviewer sees the album as proof that he was more than Coltrane's man.
werk/mccoy-tyner-the-real-mccoy.listen: In Passion Dance, listen to the trance-like rhythm with which the record opens and notice how the band sustains that feeling from beginning to end.

werk/mccoy-tyner-today-and-tomorrow.text:
Today and Tomorrow is pianist McCoy Tyner's fifth album as a leader. It was released on the Impulse! label and came about in two sessions, in 1963 and 1964. In June 1963 Tyner played in a trio, with bassist Jimmy Garrison and drummer Albert Heath. In February 1964 a sextet followed, with tenor saxophonist John Gilmore, trumpeter Thad Jones, alto saxophonist Frank Strozier, bassist Butch Warren and drummer Elvin Jones.

Because of those two line-ups, the album is varied. Contemporary Focus, T 'N A Blues and Three Flowers come from the sextet session. A Night in Tunisia, Autumn Leaves and When Sunny Gets Blue were recorded by the trio. The American critic Scott Yanow wrote on AllMusic that this record offers more variety than most of the pianist's Impulse recordings.
werk/mccoy-tyner-today-and-tomorrow.listen: Listen to A Night in Tunisia, a composition by Dizzy Gillespie, and notice how the pianist plays the piece with only bass and drums.

werk/mercedes-sosa-la-voz-de-la-zafra.text:
La voz de la zafra is Mercedes Sosa's debut album. It was recorded in 1961 and released in 1962 by RCA Victor Argentina. The original release contained twelve songs, eight of them by Armando Tejada Gómez and Manuel Óscar Matus, her husband. The record later appeared in several countries under other titles, such as Canta Mercedes Sosa and Mercedes Sosa.

The album is regarded as a forerunner of the Movimiento del Nuevo Cancionero in Argentina. The Argentine Ministry of Culture wrote that this record and her second album, Canciones con fundamento, established her on the Latin American stage. This was due not only to the quality of her voice and singing, but also to her great social commitment as a founder of that movement.
werk/mercedes-sosa-la-voz-de-la-zafra.listen: Listen to La Zafrera, one of the songs by Tejada Gómez and Matus, and notice how her voice carries the song.

werk/meshell-ndegeocello-bitter.text:
Bitter is Meshell Ndegeocello's third album and was released on 24 August 1999 on Maverick Records. Craig Street produced it, and it was recorded at Mad Dog Studios in Burbank. Besides her own vocals and bass guitar, Lisa Coleman and Wendy Melvoin, among others, play on it, there is a string quartet, and David Torn and Doyle Bramhall II play guitar. There is also a song by Jimi Hendrix on it, May This Be Love.

The reviews varied widely. Billboard wrote of a modern masterpiece, and Vibe called it album of the year. The New York Times saw rhythms guided by her bass playing, with guitars, strings and her restrained singing interlocking like brain waves. Others were less enthusiastic: the Chicago Tribune heard a bittersweet sadness, and the Hartford Courant found it dull. On the Billboard 200 the album reached number 105.
werk/meshell-ndegeocello-bitter.listen: Listen to May This Be Love and notice how the bass carries the tempo and the mood. Can you hear how restrained the vocals remain?

werk/meshell-ndegeocello-cookie-the-anth.text:
Cookie: The Anthropological Mixtape is Meshell Ndegeocello's fourth album and was released on 4 June 2002 on Maverick Records. Her third album, Bitter, sold poorly, and the record company now wanted a record that sounded more like a black record. She worked with, among others, Talib Kweli, Missy Elliott and Tweet, and with her own band, the Conscientious Objectors. Recording in the summer of 2001 took about a month, at Hyde Street Studios in San Francisco. She took the mixtapes of her youth as her model.

The album blends hip hop, funk, soul, jazz and go-go. Between the tracks are excerpts from speeches by Angela Davis and Gil Scott-Heron. The lyrics deal with consumption, revolution, religion and love between women. Because of lyrics that were linked to 9/11, the release was postponed several times. Critics were very positive, and the album received a Grammy nomination.
werk/meshell-ndegeocello-cookie-the-anth.listen: Listen to Hot Night and notice Talib Kweli's rap and the excerpts from Angela Davis. Can you hear how the bass in the bridge sounds like a ticking time bomb?

werk/metallica-and-justice-for-all.text:
...And Justice for All is Metallica's fourth studio album and was released on 7 September 1988 on Elektra Records. It is the first record with bassist Jason Newsted, after Cliff Burton died in 1986. Burton is credited posthumously as co-writer of To Live Is to Die. Recording took four months at One on One Recording Studios in Los Angeles, with producer Flemming Rasmussen. A first attempt with Mike Clink did not go well.

The music is fast and complex, with long tracks, many changing riffs and little verse and chorus structure. The lyrics deal with political and legal injustice, corruption, censorship and war. One, with the band's first music video, received a great deal of airplay. Critics praised the depth, but criticised the dry mix and the almost inaudible bass guitar. In 1989 the record was nominated for a Grammy.
werk/metallica-and-justice-for-all.listen: Listen to Harvester of Sorrow and try to hear Jason Newsted's bass guitar: how far is it buried in the mix?

werk/metallica-death-magnetic.text:
After the raw St. Anger, Metallica chose a new producer: Rick Rubin. He had the band finish the songs almost completely first and then record them as if it were a live performance. Recording ran from March 2007 to May 2008 in studios around Los Angeles. Robert Trujillo played as bassist for the first time.

The album sounds like a return to the thrash metal of old, with more intricate compositions, standard guitar tuning and long solos by Kirk Hammett and James Hetfield. Suicide & Redemption is the first instrumental track since Orion from 1986. Critics saw a return to form, but found the production too heavily compressed. My Apocalypse won a Grammy for Best Metal Performance.
werk/metallica-death-magnetic.listen: Listen to Suicide & Redemption and follow how the guitars do the work without a singer. Where do you hear a solo?
